title: A credit books to the inventory part's current category
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit', 'Work Orders — Order Parts' and 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit'.
  • Use staging with the QuickBooks sandbox connected, and sign in to that QuickBooks sandbox in a second browser window.
  • Have a new category for this test, category A, priced by a new matrix for this test, matrix A, with one cost range ($0.00 and up) whose Default rule is Markup % 35, mapped to a QuickBooks item for this test, item A.
  • Have a new category for this test, category B, priced by a new matrix for this test, matrix B, with , mapped to a different QuickBooks item, item B.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, left on Default for work orders and Part Sales.
  • Have a new inventory part for this test at your location, in category A, cost $100.00.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer B, made after customer B's tier was set, with one labor line (line 1), with that inventory part on line 1 at $135.00, invoiced and synced.
  • Make sure the inventory part was moved to category B after the invoice synced.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so every column of the page shows.
custom_steps:
1. Make a credit for the part line from work order 1's invoice.
  2. Open the credit in the QuickBooks sandbox once it has synced.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • A credit for the part is made and syncs.

Step 2:

  • The QuickBooks credit line uses item B, mapped to category B, the part's current category.
  • It does not use item A of category A.
